Documentation → Automation & Change Control → Wiki → Confluence

Wiki → Confluence — publish articles to a Confluence space

Publish a Wiki article's published version to Confluence, one way, as a page SATOM keeps updating; administrators set up the connection in Settings → Integrations, the publisher picks the space and the parent page from the article's Confluence button, and a credential scan and an audience check run before anything leaves.

👤 ForOperatorAdministrator
🔑 Permissionswiki.write wiki.moderate
📍 WhereThe Confluence button on each Wiki article (list card and article page); connections in Settings → Integrations → Confluence (URL /settings/integrations/#confluence)

What is it?#

A Wiki article can be published to Confluence, one way: SATOM writes the page, Confluence never writes back, and the page is replaced each time the article is published there again. The page's last line says so and links back to the article in SATOM. Confluence Cloud (REST API v2) and Confluence Data Center / Server are supported.

Where is it?#

  • The Confluence button on each article's card in the Wiki list and on the article page, for its author and the moderators, once a connection is enabled. A number next to it says how many Confluence pages the article already has.
  • Settings → Integrations → Confluence (administrators): the connections — address, account and credential. Until 2026-10-23 this was Wiki → Confluence; old links land on the new card.

How to use#

Set up a connection (administrator)#

  1. Create the credential in Confluence: on Cloud, an API token for the account that will own the pages (id.atlassian.com → Security → API tokens); on Data Center, a personal access token. Give that account permission to add pages in the spaces you will publish to.
  2. Open Settings → Integrations and fill New connection in the Confluence card:
Field
Name how the publishing dialog names it when there are several
Confluence Cloud (REST API v2) or Data Center / Server
Address https://<site>.atlassian.net/wiki on Cloud (/wiki is added for an atlassian.net address), or the Data Center base address. https:// only
Authentication User + API token (Cloud: the account's e-mail) or Personal access token
API token / password write-only
  1. Save, then Test: it lists the spaces the account sees and says how many. 0 means the account reaches Confluence but sees no space.

There is no space or parent page on the connection: whoever publishes picks them.

Publish an article#

  1. Publish the article in the Wiki first: only a published version goes, never a draft.
  2. Press Confluence on its card or on the article.
  3. Pick the Space (the box above it filters the list). The Connection list only shows when there are several.
  4. Pick the Parent page: the space's tree opens at its top level — open a page's arrow to see the pages under it — or type in Search the pages of this space to find one by title (each hit shows the pages above it). Click the page the new one goes under; Top level of the space is the default.
  5. If the article is limited to ADOMs, profiles or groups, tick The readers of that Confluence space may read it: Confluence knows nothing of SATOM's audience.
  6. Press Publish version N.

The first publication to a space creates a page. Later ones to the same space update that page (by its id) with the next Confluence version, even if its title changed or someone moved it: the button reads Update to version N and the dialog says the parent is not used. Publishing to another space creates a second page there.

Already in Confluence, at the top of the dialog, lists each page with its space, the version it holds and whether it is up to date. Forget stops updating a page and leaves it in Confluence.

Credential check#

Before publishing, the title, description and text are scanned for what looks like a credential: private keys, cloud, Git, Slack, Atlassian and JSON Web tokens, FortiOS set … ENC … secrets, user:password@ in an address, Authorization: headers, and password: …-style values that are not placeholders (<password>, ${VAR}, ****, changeme). Findings are listed by kind and line — never the value — in the dialog, and they stop the publication. Remove them and publish again. A moderator who has checked that they are not credentials may tick the override; that is audited.

Safety#

  • The credential is kept like every SATOM secret: in the vault when one is configured, otherwise encrypted, and it is never shown again. Changing a connection's address, flavour, authentication or user removes it, so an edit can never send a stored credential somewhere new.
  • Listing spaces and pages is part of publishing: only the article's author and the moderators can do it, and only through an enabled connection. Only the words of a search reach Confluence's query language (CQL).
  • Calls go through the same checked path as Plugin Studio connections: no address of the node itself, its HA peer, loopback or link-local; the checked address is the one dialled; redirects are not followed; the credential is removed from every error message.
  • Raw HTML in the article stays text, unsafe links are removed, links to SATOM pages become plain text (they mean nothing in Confluence), and images are linked by their address.
  • Every publication, refusal, Forget and connection change is written to the Audit log (wiki.confluence.*).
  • Deleting an article or a connection in SATOM leaves its pages in Confluence.

Permissions#

Permission Allows
wiki.write publish your own published articles through an enabled connection
wiki.moderate publish any article; override a credential warning
user_manage (administrator) set up, test and delete connections (Settings → Integrations)

Troubleshooting#

Symptom Cause and fix
No Confluence button on an article You are not its author or a moderator, the article is not published, or no connection is enabled.
"Confluence refused the credential (HTTP 401)" Wrong e-mail/token pair, an expired token, or a Data Center token used as User + API token. Enter the credential again in Settings → Integrations.
The space list is empty, or Test says 0 spaces The account cannot see any space: give it access in Confluence.
The tree shows "No pages under this one." That page has no child pages; pick it, or another one.
The parent page picker does not show The article already has a page in that space: publishing updates it where it is. Forget it first to create a new one elsewhere.
"A page with this title may already exist in the space" Confluence titles are unique per space. Rename the article or the existing page.
"The article looks like it holds credentials" Remove them (or, for a moderator, override after checking). The message gives kind and line.
"Confluence could not be reached: … refused" The address resolves to this node, its HA peer, loopback or link-local, which SATOM never calls.
"Confluence answered with a redirect to …" Set the connection's address to where it points (often /wiki missing).
The credential disappeared after an edit The address, flavour, authentication or user changed: enter it again.
Edits made in Confluence are gone Publishing is one way: the next publication replaces the page. Edit in SATOM.
Wiki → Confluence is gone from the Wiki menu Connections moved to Settings → Integrations → Confluence (administrators).
